After months of Liquid Glass testing, WhatsApp is expanding the redesigned interface of its iPad app, adding a brand-new Mac-like sidebar. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp initially began adapting its iOS app to the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul last October, it was not until later — specifically June of last year — that the company brought the redesigned interface to the iPad and started limited beta testing.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the redesign included Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and contextual menus, while retaining the same bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

Now, the site reports that WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the bottom tab bar by default with a brand-new Mac-like sidebar.

This sidebar adopts the same layout already found in the WhatsApp Mac version, providing quick access to Chats, Status, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to give the chat list and conversation view more room.

Here's the report:

WABetaInfo noted that beta testers running the latest TestFlight version already have access to the new sidebar, although some users on the regular App Store version have also started seeing this new interface.

As is typical of WhatsApp's rollout approach, whether users are on the beta or stable version of the app, the new interface may take some time to reach everyone. Once it becomes available to iPad users, however, they should benefit from this more tablet-friendly layout.
